plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Endless ribbons of violet-blue spikes ripple across sun-baked hillsides, releasing a warm, herbal perfume that hums with bees. In Provence the rows of silvery-green foliage seem to melt into the horizon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with true lavender at its best from late June to mid-July
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used the flowers to scent their baths.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dinner-plate-sized crown of silky pink bracts surrounds a downy center, like a thistle built for royalty. In the Southern Hemisphere winter it brings bold color to the fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly July to October, which includes the start of the Southern Hemisphere winter flowering season
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. It is also an ancient lineage, and its fire-resistant rootstock lets it resprout after bushfires.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge, cupped blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repelling leaves. Each flower opens at dawn and closes at dusk, and the show drifts across ponds and lakes through high summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, around June and July in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across temperate and subtropical Asia, and in gardens in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves shed water and dirt in tiny beads, a self-cleaning effect scientists call the 'lotus effect'. It has inspired water-repellent materials.
